title: Rapamycin Side Effects: Complete Safety Guide | BodySpec
abstract: This guide unpacks the latest evidence on **rapamycin side effects**, showing how they change with dose, frequency, and personal risk factors—then offers practical monitoring and mitigation steps you can discuss with your physician. | Organ transplant immunosuppression | 2–5 mg **daily** (target trough > 5 ng/mL) | Continuous | Prevent rejection | **High** — mouth ulcers, impaired wound healing, infections, cytopenias, metabolic issues |. | Longevity / biohacking | 4–10 mg **weekly** or 1 mg every other day (target trough < 3 ng/mL) | Intermittent | Lower mTORC1 without hitting mTORC2 | **Low–moderate** — most effects are transient and manageable (patient-reported longevity dosing data) |. Since many reported side effects originate from the high-dose transplant setting, separating these regimens is step one in realistic risk assessment. ## Side-Effect Risk by Dose & Frequency. 1. **Side effects scale with dose and exposure time.** Weekly or bi-weekly dosing keeps most risks low.
